findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the new [tool.rebar.jira] mapping sub-tables avoid the existing unknown-key warn/error path (`_warn_unknown` / `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error`) — e.g. route the mapping block through a reserved-section carve-out like `llm.*` or a dedicated sub-table the typed JiraConfig ignores — so a present block neither warns nor hard-fails.
evidence: _config_schema.py:57-74 `_warn_unknown` WARNs on leftover keys, `strict=True` (REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error) raises ConfigError
JiraConfig declares only url/user/project/allow_insecure (_config_schema.py:511-529)
docs/config.md:370-377: the llm.* block required an explicit 'reserved section' carve-out so the core loader 'never warns on it (nor rejects it under REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error)'
Plan quote: 'Absent block ⇒ empty overlay (today's behavior)' — but a PRESENT block of new keys would not be today's behavior; it would warn or hard-fail
findings.finding: The plan parses its new mapping sub-tables (default, projects.<KEY>, status_map, type_map, link_map, priority_map, create_defaults, statuses, issue_types, link_types, hierarchy) under the existing [tool.rebar.jira] block, but does not address the codebase's unknown-key policy: the current loader coerces [tool.rebar.jira] into the typed JiraConfig (declared fields url/user/project/allow_insecure) and _warn_unknown() WARNS on leftover keys, escalating to a hard ConfigError under REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error. The new keys would trip that path unless explicitly reserved/routed, as the llm.* section had to be.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('Parses an optional [tool.rebar.jira] mapping block'); AC1
scenarios: An operator adds [tool.rebar.jira.default.status_map] and every rebar invocation logs 'unknown key ignored' warnings
A store running REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error (the post-deprecation cutover) hard-fails at config load the moment any mapping key is present
findings.suggested_fix: Model the mapping block as a reserved section the core typed loader recognises but does not coerce into JiraConfig (the docs/config.md:370-377 llm.* precedent), and have load_mapping_config read that reserved sub-tree; document it in docs/config.md alongside the shape.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the validation exception class (e.g. `MappingConfigError`) in Scope/Approach so `test_validate_fails_closed` can assert on the exact error type.
evidence: 'a status_map value not in the declared statuses set raises a named error'
'validate fails closed offline on: a value outside the declared vocabulary ... each asserted on the exact error'
No exception class name appears anywhere in Scope or Approach
findings.finding: AC4 and the testing section require validation to 'raise a named error' but the plan never specifies the exception class name/type, leaving the executor to invent it and the test to assert on an unspecified target.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (validate fails closed) / Testing (Fail-closed validation)
scenarios: Executor writes test_validate_fails_closed and must guess whether to raise ValueError, a custom MappingConfigError, etc.; the 'assert on the exact error' requirement is unactionable without a named type.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: a `MappingConfigError` (or similarly named) exception raised by `validate`, and reference it by name in AC4 and the testing section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the new `Capability` descriptor with the existing `_backend.py` capability Protocols (SupportsLinks/SupportsComments) and cc77 narrowing: state explicitly why an offline axis-declaration dataclass is a distinct concern from the runtime isinstance capability checks, and whether the adapter derives one from the other to avoid two drifting truth-sources.
evidence: _backend.py docstring: 'plus zero or more opt-in capability Protocols (SupportsLinks, SupportsComments)'; 'Callers detect a capability by an isinstance-guarded check against the backend'
_backend.py:637 'Capability narrowing (ticket cc77)' — hasattr-attributed opt-in transport members

The plan's Capability is offline/static (axis-declaration for config validation) whereas the existing mechanism is behavioral/runtime (isinstance on a live client) — a real distinction, but the naming and concept overlap is unaddressed
findings.finding: The plan's `Capability` descriptor dataclass (has_types/has_transitions/has_hierarchy/has_link_types) is not reconciled against the existing capability mechanism in `_backend.py` (the @runtime_checkable opt-in Protocols `SupportsLinks`/`SupportsComments` and the cc77 hasattr-based transport-capability narrowing), which also expresses 'which axes/features a backend supports'.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer conflates the two 'capability' concepts, or a third capability truth-source drifts from the backend Protocols

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the new `[tool.rebar.jira].projects.<KEY>` config tables relate to the existing per-project store mapping (.bridge_state/projects.json, ADR 0097): whether keys must agree, what a key present in one but not the other means, and which surface owns per-project mapping data — and document this in the docs/config.md update.
evidence: docs/config.md: '.bridge_state/projects.json on the tickets branch ... a property of the store, not of any one repo'; shape '{"projects": {"REB": {"repos": ["rebar"]}}}' — an existing per-project keyed mapping

docs/config.md: 'the projects a store actively syncs are added through the mapping rather than through config' — an explicit statement that per-project data lives in the store mapping, which the plan's config-side projects.<KEY> block partially duplicates in surface shape
findings.finding: The plan introduces a `projects.<KEY>` per-project keyed config surface under [tool.rebar.jira] without relating it to the already-documented per-project store mapping (.bridge_state/projects.json, ADR 0097), risking a second, potentially-divergent per-project surface.
scenarios: A project key present in [tool.rebar.jira].projects but absent from projects.json (or vice versa); an operator unsure which per-project surface owns what

findings.finding: The plan attributes the concrete-backends-import-core one-way dependency rule to 'ADR 0035', but in this repo ADR 0035 is 'Snapshot-horizon-safe replay: conservative fold horizon + rebuild-on-stray (RC2b)'. The reconciler vendor-adapter seam ADR (which actually documents the seam and one-way dependency direction) was renumbered from 0035 to 0083 by story 0743 because three ADRs collided on number 0035; the ADRs themselves warn 'a bare ADR 0035 is ambiguous in this repo'. The substance of the claim (concrete backends import shared/core via _backend.py, never the reverse) is real and enforced, but the citation number is stale/ambiguous.
findings.location: Approach §4 / final paragraph ('This respects the ADR 0035 one-way dependency direction (`_backend.py`: ...)')
scenarios: A reader/implementer opens docs/adr/0035-*.md to check the dependency-direction rule and lands on the snapshot-replay ADR, finding nothing about the vendor seam.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'This respects the ADR 0035 one-way dependency direction' with 'This respects the ADR 0083 (formerly 0035) reconciler vendor-adapter seam one-way dependency direction'.
